description: Introduce a minimal browser-based testing foundation for Family Pulse so user-critical visual and DOM-driven behaviors can be verified automatically. Add one browser test runner, stable app bootstrapping against the test database, reusable auth helpers, and a small set of end-to-end flows focused on current high-risk pages such as Reports.

timing.gatingCondition: Feature 17 should land first so Reports page chart behavior and its acceptance criteria are stable enough to target.

principles: Browser tests should complement node:test rather than replace it
Start with a small, reliable set of user-critical flows instead of broad UI coverage
The test harness must work with the existing seeded test database and local app startup model
Stability matters more than visual exhaustiveness in the first release
Selectors and fixtures should be intentional so UI refactors do not cause excessive churn

techStack.browserTesting: Playwright with Chromium as the initial supported browser
techStack.database: Existing PostgreSQL test database seeded via current test scripts
techStack.testing: Playwright for selected end-to-end flows; keep node:test for API and business logic coverage

userStories.title: Establish a browser test harness that boots the app reliably
acceptanceCriteria: The repo gains a documented browser test runner configuration
Browser tests can start the app against test configuration without manual setup beyond installed dependencies
The harness reuses the existing test database reset/migrate/seed flow or a clearly documented equivalent
Local and CI execution paths are both defined
The initial implementation supports one browser target only to keep scope tight
userStories.testStrategy: Manual smoke run of the browser harness plus one passing end-to-end spec in local dev.

userStories.title: Provide reusable browser auth/session helpers
acceptanceCriteria: Tests can authenticate as a parent without duplicating low-level session setup in each spec
The auth helper works with the current family_members and sessions model
Tests can land directly on protected pages in an authenticated state
The setup avoids requiring interactive login form entry for every spec
userStories.testStrategy: End-to-end test uses helper-backed authenticated page access.

userStories.title: Cover the Reports page with a focused browser spec
acceptanceCriteria: A browser test verifies that a parent can load reports.html and see the chart sections
The doughnut month selector can change months without breaking the chart area
Theme toggle can be exercised and the page remains readable and interactive afterward
Ask Pulse or What-If history refresh behavior is covered at the page level
The spec asserts behavior and state, not pixel-perfect canvas output
userStories.testStrategy: Playwright spec with seeded data and stable selectors.

userStories.title: Cover one additional non-chart user-critical flow
acceptanceCriteria: At least one more page outside Reports has browser coverage
The chosen flow represents a common user path such as budget page load, transaction filtering, or settings access
The test validates real DOM interaction rather than only page load success
userStories.testStrategy: Playwright spec against a second page with one real interaction.

userStories.title: Document browser testing scope and non-goals
acceptanceCriteria: The feature documents when to use browser tests vs node:test
The first release explicitly avoids broad screenshot regression testing
Selector conventions and fixture expectations are documented
Running the browser tests locally is documented in the repo
userStories.testStrategy: Documentation review plus successful local run using the documented commands.

high: Browser tests can become flaky quickly if selectors, seed data, and app startup are not standardized from the start
medium: Canvas-heavy pages like Reports are harder to assert directly, so tests need behavior-focused expectations
Test runtime will increase once the app is booted in a browser harness
low: One-browser support may miss browser-specific issues initially, but it keeps the first release maintainable

preFlightChecklist: Confirm whether Playwright is acceptable as the first non-zero test dependency
Define how the app should boot under browser tests using test env vars and seeded DB state
Choose the first non-chart page to cover in addition to Reports
Identify stable selectors or add test ids only where necessary
Decide whether browser tests run in default CI or only in a dedicated job initially

executionSlices.name: Slice A: Harness setup
executionSlices.goal: Add Playwright config, scripts, and app bootstrapping against the test environment.
notes: Reuse existing test DB preparation where possible

executionSlices.name: Slice B: Auth and fixtures
executionSlices.goal: Create reusable helpers for parent-authenticated browser sessions and stable seeded entry points.
notes: Avoid typing through login UI in every spec
Keep setup aligned with the current sessions table model

executionSlices.name: Slice C: Initial end-to-end flows
executionSlices.goal: Add a Reports spec and one additional page-level spec that validate real DOM behavior.
notes: Exercise theme toggle, selectors, and one data-refresh flow

executionSlices.name: Slice D: Documentation and boundaries
executionSlices.goal: Document when browser tests should be used and what remains out of scope.
notes: Do not attempt broad visual regression in the first release
Keep node:test as the default path for non-browser logic

primaryGoals: Catch regressions that only appear after real page load, DOM updates, theme changes, responsive layout changes, or user interaction
Reduce repetitive manual QA for high-value flows on visual pages
initialCoverage: Month selector interaction on the doughnut chart
History refresh after Ask Pulse or What-If submission
One additional flow on budget, transactions, or settings
nonGoals: Pixel-perfect screenshot baselines for all visual states
Replacing current node:test API and unit coverage
